# Automatic HTTP capture fixtures

The protocol payloads in `test/agent-usage-http-capture.test.ts` and `test/agent-usage-capture-host.test.ts` are hand-authored synthetic fixtures. They contain no account responses, personal logs, credentials, project contents or copied third-party implementation.

Shapes exercised:

- OpenAI Responses `response.completed` with `response.id`, `output` function calls and cumulative `usage`; reference: https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/responses-streaming/response/completed
- OpenAI Chat completion stream `choices[].delta.tool_calls` indexed argument fragments, a cumulative usage chunk, and `[DONE]`; reference: https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/chat/create
- Anthropic Messages `message_start`, `content_block_start`, `content_block_delta`, `message_delta`, `message_stop`; reference: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/api/messages-streaming
- Claude native assistant usage uses existing fixture provenance in `provider-logs/PROVENANCE.md`, with synthetic message IDs shared with capture to test reconciliation.

The fake provider in `test/runtime.test.ts` consumes the actual environment prefix and managed runtime command generated by `AcpxAgentRuntime`, replacing only the provider executable with a controlled local Node script. An explicit guard refuses execution unless the fake-script path is present. The fake follows configured Codex `CODEX_CONFIG` / Claude `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and sends requests solely to controlled loopback servers. This proves service runtime configuration and Run reuse wiring; it is not live Provider or billing acceptance.
